- Overweight recent sentiment spikes in the 1-3 day window when forecasting short-term (next 7-14 days) — model tends to overreact.
- Underweight sentiment when it’s negative and persistent (e.g., -0.2 to -0.9) — model often ignores bearish sentiment, leading to overestimation.
- When sentiment is high and price is trending up, model tends to overshoot by 2-5% in the first 5-7 days — apply a 1-2% downward correction.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.5–0.7) and price is consolidating, model often overpredicts — reduce forecast by 1-3% for next 10-15 days.
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the 15-30 day horizon when sentiment is weak or mixed — apply a 2-4% downward bias for longer-term forecasts.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative after a spike, model fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 3-5% immediately after sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 15-30 day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1-3% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment history with repeated +0.65–1.56 spikes often leads to model overcorrection — cap forecast at 10% below peak if sentiment remains high.
